Before further investment, Matt conducted an architecture assessment and gap/fit analysis. He reviewed code, interviewed stakeholders, analyzed documentation, and assessed Data, Application, Technology, and Business Architecture. Drawing on prior WebSeries implementation experience, he created architectural heat maps showing where the platform fell short. He worked with the bank’s enterprise architecture team on logical and system models, with a transparent cost-to-fix versus benefit comparison.

The assessment found that WebSeries lacked the modularity required for **RBC’s** long-term digital operating model. That finding prevented investment in a platform path that could not deliver what the bank needed and enabled technical resources to move to higher-priority initiatives. The heat maps and roadmap artifacts remained reference material for future modernization planning.

Matt also established the PMO, coordinating **3 organizations**: **RBC**, **Accenture**, and Bottomline Technologies. He maintained the program roadmap and dependencies, introduced designated team contacts and daily summaries, and built a task-tracking matrix. Centralized communications eliminated missed program updates; task tracking reduced redundant work and clarified assignments. He also managed engagement margin and staffing, bringing in senior and specialized resources early, then transitioning work offshore and nearshore as it became repeatable.

For mobile readiness, Matt defined API integration points, cheque-deposit requirements, and cross-browser and cross-device scalability needs. He delivered a modernization blueprint for mobile adoption and real-time account access. The recorded outcomes are assessment, governance, and architecture deliverables, not a production mobile launch or quantified savings.
